constraint: this whole system is really just a public-records machine that turns a messy PDF ordinance into defensible data consumers actually want and trust. It took us building literally everything up to this point to make it work; that doesn't mean it should only work like this; its additive in nature; agents reproduce recursively have a net positive value; coordination costs negligible; this could be done with more lanes and subagents without issue. Explore broadly, think freely, no boundaries / limitations for the analysis; instead of allowing rules to box in innovation, use rules to set the foundation and lower bound of what MUST be accomplished, without setting a ceiling; operate in good faith toward the goal; want to give agents the opportunity to explore the spaces between the rules and look for opportunities to innovate in structure and design of data; we want them to think top-down and bottom-up simultaneously, both zoomed in to the details and zoomed out to the structure and macro picture as a fractal; looking for local innovations that scale globally given existing structures and data model; especially as we build new features and functions from data we currently are only partially serving through our product; lots of value to capture

countingRuleReconciliation.resolution: both are right and they count different units. The census counts city ROWS, one per county, so a city spanning two counties is counted twice: 61 rows. Distinct city slugs = 54. Recomputed by _inbox/2026-09-16_p258_wavegen.mjs from the census arrays: cityRows=61, distinctCities=54. Six cities span two counties: mustang-ridge-tx, uhland-tx, niederwald-tx, creedmoor-tx, webberville-tx, coupland-tx (61 - 6 = 55; one further pair is inside a single county, so the measured 54 is the number of record and is what the worklist carries with its rule).

preRegisteredFalsifiers.statement: Every one of the 209 units and 54 cities appears in the worklist with a state; none is silently missing.
preRegisteredFalsifiers.answerRegisteredBeforeWork: PASS by construction for presence: the worklist is generated from the census, so every entry exists before any lane runs. The falsifier as literally worded can still FAIL on `state`, because a lane that never runs, or that runs and forgets an entry, leaves `pending`. Grading rule: count entries whose state is still `pending` at close. Any non-zero count is a FAIL of F1, reported with the entries named.

preRegisteredFalsifiers.statement: Every acquired row cites an instrument and an effective date read at source.
preRegisteredFalsifiers.answerRegisteredBeforeWork: PASS requires, per acquired table: (a) a citation_url that resolves at the time it is recorded, (b) an instrument named (ordinance number, code chapter, or document title), (c) an effective date READ at source (ordinance adoption/effective date, or an ArcGIS editingInfo.lastEditDate) and never assumed from the source kind, and (d) a per-value section_number plus a verbatim quote. Grading rule: I re-fetch a sample of cited URLs myself and substring-match the quotes. A single acquired row with an instrument but no read-at-source date is a FAIL of F2, reported with the row named. `primary-source-verified` is accepted as the verification_state where no code-section atom corpus exists, which is the belton/seguin/cibolo precedent, not a lower standard invented here.

preRegisteredFalsifiers.statement: No planned-development code gets a Euclidean table row.
preRegisteredFalsifiers.answerRegisteredBeforeWork: PASS requires a mechanical check over every table the wave adds or edits: no district row whose name or code matches the PUD/PDD/PD/PC family, and no unit in the out-of-scope half. Grading rule: I run the check myself over the wave's diffs and over the worklist, counting PUD-class units as out-of-scope-pud rather than acquired. The 61,725 planned-development parcels are A-164's PUD message (P-256/P-257), not acquisition.

preRegisteredFalsifiers.statement: Pre-registered band: how much of the wave can actually be acquired.
preRegisteredFalsifiers.answerRegisteredBeforeWork: I register, before any lane runs, that the district-miss half (batch 1) is acquirable and the no-table half (batch 2) is mostly not, and I state the bands so a result outside them is a finding either way (DEV_PROCESS 4.5). Bands of acquired units at close: lane-a 20 to 50 of 50 (Austin's dimensional standards are one instrument, so the mechanism should reach most units); lane-b 6 to 16 of 16; lane-c 10 to 60 of 143; lane-d/e/f acquired city tables 0 to 6 of 61 rows, with 40 to 61 rows classified and stated. A result BELOW a band is the expected finding (research is slower than the dispatch assumes). A result ABOVE a band is the finding that needs the most scrutiny, because this program's defect class is a plausible-looking value nobody checked.
